title: Gradient Compression May Hurt Generalization: A Remedy by Synthetic Data Guided Sharpness Aware Minimization
main_claims: Gradient compression in federated learning induces sharper loss landscapes, especially under non-IID data distributions, hindering generalization.
Direct application of SAM in FL suffers from inaccurate global perturbation estimation due to data heterogeneity, and this problem is worsened with gradient compression.
FedSynSAM, which uses synthetic data derived from global model trajectory matching to estimate the true global perturbation, outperforms existing federated SAM methods.
methodology: The paper first empirically shows gradient compression increases Hessian top eigenvalues (sharpness) in FedAvg. Then FedSynSAM is proposed, using dataset distillation via trajectory matching on the server to construct synthetic data that approximates global gradient statistics, enabling accurate SAM perturbation estimation. Convergence bounds are derived and experiments are run on CIFAR-10/100 with various compression schemes.
key_results: 4-bit quantization increases Hessian top eigenvalue from 7.56 to 8.82 under IID; 8-bit quantization increases from 17.04 to 17.78 under Dir(0.01) non-IID.
FedSynSAM achieves higher cosine similarity between estimated and true global perturbation than FedLESAM across all tested settings.
FedSynSAM consistently outperforms FedLESAM and FedSAM baselines in accuracy experiments.
limitations: Trajectory matching for synthetic data generation adds server-side computational overhead.
Experiments limited to image classification; broader applicability untested.
Convergence analysis relies on standard FL assumptions that may not hold in practice.
relevance_to_rq: This paper is tangentially relevant — it demonstrates that SAM improves generalization in federated settings with data corruptions/shifts, indirectly supporting the claim that SAM's flat-minima bias helps under distribution shift. However, it focuses on federated learning with gradient compression, not CIFAR-C OOD benchmarks or representation stability, so it is peripheral to the RQ.

key_quotes.text: we find that gradient compression may lead to sharper loss landscapes, suggesting that the models tend to suffer from degradation in generalization performance.
key_quotes.context: Key finding motivating the paper: compression induces sharpness

key_quotes.text: the direct application of SAM in FL suffers from inaccurate estimation of the global perturbation due to data heterogeneity.
key_quotes.context: Limitation of naive FedSAM motivating FedSynSAM

key_quotes.text: FedSynSAM utilizes a synthetic dataset, derived via trajectory matching without requiring extra information beyond the global model trajectory, to facilitate a more accurate estimation of the true global perturbation.

related_work_mentioned: Sharpness-Aware Minimization for Efficiently Improving Generalization
